answer: A data market named atlas could view agent identities through the prism of scarce storage, rather than names. To earn a provider slot, each agent must commit to a distinct randomly assigned data shard and answer unpredictable possession checks. An oasis of aliases then requires proportionally more retained data and bandwidth; one shard cannot satisfy every identity. Attackers pay storage and retrieval costs, but outsourced storage, hardware advantages and dishonest challenge generation remain limitations.
